newsitem.title: USA: Army told to pay damages in sex harassment case.
newsitem.headline: Army told to pay damages in sex harassment case.

text.p: A judge recommended on Tuesday that the Army pay $300,000 in damages to a former Fort Bliss employee who alleged she was sexually harassed by a colonel, Army officials said.

Ann Fuller, an administrative judge with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, said Col. Allen Hasbrouck forced subordinate Peggy Graham into sexual acts over a period of several years, telling her her job would be in jeopardy if she did not comply.

Graham, who alleged she was harassed from 1988 to 1994, worked as an administrative assistant to Hasbrouck at Fort Bliss in the west Texas border city of El Paso. She said she was happy with the judge's recommendation that she be paid $300,000 in damages plus her medical and legal costs.
"What I mainly wanted is for the Army and this man to own up to what was done to me," Graham said.
The Army had previously conducted an internal investigation and sent Hasbrouck a letter of reprimand along with an order for early retirement. He left the Army in 1994.

But Graham, who was hospitalized after an attempted suicide she said was prompted by the harassment, took the case to the EEOC. The Army now has 60 days to respond to the judge's decision or it becomes final.

Fort Bliss officials maintain the Army is not liable for damages in the case because Graham entered into a voluntary relationship with the colonel and did not follow the established internal procedures to make her complaint.
"There's a lot more to this case than seems apparent," Fort Bliss spokeswoman Jean Offutt said.
Thirteen other former and current employees of Fort Bliss have filed a class action suit against the base claiming sexual harassment. A trial date has been set for August.
